planting.note: Pot in fall into very sharply drained mineral succulent mix; Bunny Succulent is a winter grower and must be kept completely dry through summer dormancy.

directions: Grow in full sun in very sharply drained, mineral-rich succulent mix; Bunny Succulent is a winter-growing mesemb from Namaqualand, South Africa, named for its paired seedling cotyledons that strikingly resemble a pair of rabbit ears before fusing into a mature stem segment. Water only during its cool-season active growth and keep it bone dry through summer dormancy, since overwatering during the resting period quickly causes rot. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a container specimen outside true desert climates.

planting.note: Pot in fall into sharply drained succulent mix; Butter Tree leafs out in winter and drops its leaves for summer dormancy, the reverse of most garden plants.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained succulent mix, protected below about 30°F; Butter Tree is a South African caudiciform shrublet with a swollen, papery-barked trunk and leaves that emerge in winter and drop again as the plant goes summer-dormant. Water minimally during the summer rest and only somewhat more during winter active growth. All parts of the plant contain cardiac glycosides and are toxic if ingested, so site it away from pets and children and handle with that caution in mind; it is otherwise a dramatic, slow-growing container specimen for a collector's succulent bench.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a standard succulent mix; Spiral Astroloba tolerates more shade than most succulents, making it a good indoor windowsill plant.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial shade in a standard well-drained succulent mix; Spiral Astroloba is a close relative of Haworthia, forming a columnar rosette of tightly spiraled, triangular leaves. It tolerates more shade than most succulents, making it a dependable choice for a bright windowsill rather than requiring direct hot sun. Water moderately during active growth and allow the soil to dry between waterings; it has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant or greenhouse specimen across most of the United States.

planting.note: Pot the bulb mostly above the soil surface in fall into a sharply drained mix; Climbing Onion sends up a twining leafless stem each season that dies back when the bulb rests.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial shade in a sharply drained succulent mix, with the large green bulb sitting mostly above the soil surface as it does in nature. Climbing Onion is a bulbous caudiciform novelty plant that sends up a twining, leafless green stem that can climb several feet given a support, dying back to the bulb when dormant. Water while the stem is actively climbing and let the bulb rest nearly dry once it dies back. All parts are toxic if ingested, and it has no frost tolerance, so grow it strictly as a container houseplant outside the warmest zones.

planting.note: Pot in spring with the tuberous base partly exposed above the soil line, in a sharply drained succulent mix; Fockea is often grown bonsai-style for its sculptural caudex.

directions: Grow in full sun to bright partial shade in a sharply drained succulent mix, with the large tuberous base exposed above the soil line for display as a bonsai-style specimen. Fockea is a South African caudiciform vine in the milkweed family, sending out slender twining stems from its sculptural swollen tuber once established. It is drought-tolerant once mature and needs little water beyond its active growing season. It has no frost tolerance, so grow it as a container or greenhouse plant in temperate climates, bringing it indoors well before the first frost.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun; European Carrion Plant is more cold-tolerant than most stapeliads, protect only below about 40°F.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained succulent mix; European Carrion Plant is a Mediterranean stapeliad with gray-green, four-angled, toothed stems, somewhat more cold-tolerant than most of its tropical African relatives and only needing protection below about 40°F. Small star-shaped maroon flowers carry a faint carrion scent to attract fly pollinators, a classic trait of this plant family. Water sparingly and allow the soil to dry fully between waterings, since stapeliads are highly prone to rot in damp conditions.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade; like other stapeliads, Orbea melanantha is highly sensitive to overwatering.

directions: Grow in full sun to bright partial shade in sharply drained succulent mix; this low, clump-forming stapeliad bears warty, four-angled stems topped by small, near-black star-shaped flowers, among the darkest-colored blooms in the family. Water sparingly and let the soil dry completely between waterings, since this genus is highly prone to stem rot in damp conditions. It has no frost tolerance and should be grown as a container specimen brought indoors well before the first frost outside zones 9-11.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun to bright partial shade; Spotted Huernia clumps readily, filling a container over a few seasons.

directions: Grow in full sun to bright partial shade, shielded from the most intense midday sun, in sharply drained succulent mix; Spotted Huernia is a clump-forming South African stapeliad with toothed stems bearing bell-shaped, cream flowers heavily spotted with maroon that lie flat against the stem. Water sparingly and let the mix dry fully between waterings, since this genus rots quickly in damp conditions. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a container succulent brought indoors before the first frost outside the warmest zones.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun; this compact Stapelia clumps more tightly than the larger-flowered Stapelia gigantea already in the dataset.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained succulent mix; this is a compact, clumping carrion flower with grayish, four-angled stems and smaller star-shaped flowers, colored yellow with purple markings, than the much larger blooms of the widely grown Stapelia gigantea. Water sparingly and let the mix dry fully between waterings, since Stapelia stems rot quickly in damp conditions. It has no frost tolerance and should be grown as a container succulent brought indoors before the first frost outside zones 9-11.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun; like other Faucaria, keep nearly dry through summer semi-dormancy and water more in the cooler growing season.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained succulent mix; Bosscheana Tiger Jaws is a South African mesemb with paired, fleshy, toothed leaves that interlock like a jaw, giving the whole genus its common name. Bright yellow daisy-like flowers open in autumn above the foliage. Water minimally through its semi-dormant summer rest and more regularly during the cooler growing season, since overwatering in summer quickly causes rot. It has no frost tolerance, so grow it as a container succulent indoors or in a greenhouse outside the mildest zones.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in full sun; water sparingly, almost not at all during summer dormancy, mimicking its native rocky habitat.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained succulent mix; Pleiospilos simulans is a mimicry mesemb from South Africa whose paired, thick, gray-brown leaves closely resemble cracked granite pebbles, a classic camouflage adaptation against grazing animals. Bright yellow flowers appear in fall, emerging from the split between the paired leaves. Water sparingly through the growing season and withhold water almost entirely during summer dormancy, since this genus is extremely prone to rot in damp or poorly drained conditions.

planting.note: Pot in fall into a very sharply drained mineral mix in bright partial shade; Conophytum truncatum drops its old leaf layer each summer and must be kept completely dry during that dormancy.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial shade, protected from intense direct sun that can scorch its translucent surface, in a very sharply drained mineral succulent mix. Conophytum truncatum forms classic button-shaped, bilobed bodies that split to shed an old leaf layer each summer dormancy, with flowers emerging from the fissure in fall as new growth resumes. Water only during the cool active season and keep it bone dry through summer rest, since this genus is extremely rot-prone when wet during dormancy. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a collector's container succulent.

planting.note: Pot in fall into a very sharply drained mineral mix in full sun; Titanopsis is a winter grower and needs minimal water to avoid rot.

directions: Grow in full sun in a very sharply drained, mineral-heavy succulent mix; Schwantes's Titanopsis is a South African mimicry mesemb whose warty, chalky-tipped leaf clusters closely resemble a cluster of limestone rock fragments, an effective camouflage against its native rocky habitat. It is a winter grower, so water minimally during the cool active season and withhold water almost entirely during summer dormancy to avoid rot. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a collector's container succulent.

planting.note: Pot in spring with the swollen caudex partly exposed for display, in a sharply drained mineral mix in full sun; Trichodiadema can be trained bonsai-style over time.

directions: Grow in full sun in sharply drained mineral succulent mix; Trichodiadema is a dwarf shrubby mesemb with a swollen underground caudex that can be grown partly exposed above the soil for a sculptural, bonsai-style display as the plant ages. Its small leaves each bear a distinctive crown of bristles at the tip, and magenta daisy-like flowers appear through the growing season. It is drought-tolerant and needs minimal water once established, with no frost tolerance, so grow it as a container specimen outside zones 9-11.

planting.note: Pot leaf cuttings or divisions in spring into a sharply drained succulent mix in bright partial shade to full sun; this highly variable species develops a thickening caudex base with age.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to full sun in sharply drained succulent mix; Adromischus marianae is a highly variable South African leaf succulent, often showing warty or blotched gray-green leaves, with several distinct forms in cultivation. With age the base thickens into a small caudex, adding sculptural interest beyond the leaves alone. It propagates readily from leaf cuttings pressed into dry succulent mix, needs minimal water with full drying between waterings, and has no frost tolerance, grown as a houseplant or container succulent across most of the United States.
